title: Coordination, Handoffs & Dependencies
summary: Learn how teams coordinate connected work, manage dependencies, and create clear handoffs so important information and responsibility do not get lost.
objectives: Explain how dependencies connect one person's work to another person's work.
Identify the information needed for a useful handoff.
Recognize when status changes should be communicated to the team.

vocab.def: Organizing connected people, tasks, timing, and information so work can proceed effectively.
The transfer of responsibility, information, or unfinished work from one person or team to another.
A task or result that another task or person relies on.
The current condition or progress of work at a particular point in time.

sections.heading: Dependencies connect work
sections.body: Many workplace tasks cannot happen independently. One person's work may need to be completed, reviewed, approved, delivered, or documented before another person can begin.

sections.heading: Good coordination makes dependencies visible
sections.body: Teams coordinate better when they know what is happening, what is blocked, what is changing, and what another person is waiting for.

sections.heading: A handoff transfers more than a task
sections.body: Useful handoffs communicate current status, completed work, unfinished work, known risks, important decisions, relevant documentation, and the expected next step.

sections.heading: Do not let important changes stay invisible
sections.body: When a delay, error, risk, or change affects someone else's work, early communication can give the team time to adjust rather than discover the problem too late.

practice.prompt: Your task is complete, but the next worker needs one important detail to continue. Is saying only 'I'm done' a complete handoff?
practice.answer: No. The handoff should include the information the next person needs to continue responsibly.

practice.prompt: A dependency changes and another team will be affected. What should happen?
practice.answer: The affected people should receive an accurate status update early enough to adjust their work.

quiz.question: Which information belongs in a strong workplace handoff?
options: Current status, completed work, unfinished work, risks, and next steps
Only the name of the person receiving the work
Only information about tasks that went well
quiz.answer: Current status, completed work, unfinished work, risks, and next steps

lab.objective: Create a structured handoff for a simulated team project that identifies status, dependencies, completed work, unresolved issues, and next steps.

reflectionPrompt: What is one piece of information that should never be omitted when another person depends on your work?
